relevance_note: Review that gives individual-level detail for two previously published HA20 patients, e.g. 'A patient with ALPS presented with fevers, bilateral cervical lymphadenopathy, extensive skin rash, and massive hepatosplenomegaly' and the variant 'the reported p.Gln415fs (35)'.
method_note: Hand-built from a full read; a short Python script in scratch only assembled the JSON. Review (Aksentijevich & Zhou 2017). In scope: (1) 'ref (16) patient', one of Zhou et al.'s 11 patients, described only as 'initially diagnosed with SLE and presented with CNS vasculitis and idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura' (the sentence has no own citation; it follows the sentence citing (16)); (2) 'ref (35) patient', the Japanese ALPS patient. The other Zhou patients and the two Japanese entero-BD families (36, 37) appear only as group counts in Table 2 (columns 'Patients (16) (n = 11)', 'Patients (37) (n = 6)', 'Patients (36) (n = 3)') and get no rows. Table 2 column 'Patients (35) (n = 1)' is a single-patient column tied to ref (35); its 1/1 cells were used as observed for the ref (35) patient (with the column header quoted as a span); its 0/1 cells were treated as zero counts and excluded no one (left not reported), per the v4 zero-count rule. Table 2 rows 'Arthritis', 'Arthralgias', 'Myalgias' repeat the same values (merged cells) and were not used. Variant: the Figure 2 legend says 'the reported p.Gln415fs (35) should be described as p.Lys417Serfs*4' and that the deletion 'reported as c.1245_1248del' should be 'c.1249_1252del'; the originally reported strings were recorded, and the review's proposed HGVS (c.1249_1252del, p.Lys417Serfs*4) is noted here only. Zygosity left not reported: Table 1 'Heterozygous' is a general statement about HA20, not about named patients. Variant type not recorded ('four nucleotide deletion' has no matching enum class; not derived from HGVS). No variant row for the ref (16) patient: the paper prints no variant for that person (Zhou mutations only in Figure 2). 'Initially diagnosed with SLE' kept in disease_label_as_stated, not as a feature. The normal CD3+CD8+ subpopulations were recorded as an excluded abnormality (D-27). No contradictions found.
